summary: All 5 target claims (A-E) critiqued side by side. 1 of 5 (D, motor-ID 7/8/9 mapping) was strengthened and effectively resolved by primary-source code inspection, overturning the brief's own hedge that it might be a vendor-specific note. 1 of 5 (A, implied smooth/low-friction build) was partially overturned: three independent GitHub artifacts (issue #17, PR #9, PR #26) show real design-level friction the brief's 'no independent friction account' framing missed, though none rise to the specific failure modes (warping/breakage/heat-set) the brief enumerated, so that narrower claim survives. 3 of 5 (B heat-set inserts, C time estimates, E real-world spend vs. baseline) held only in the weak sense of 'no counter-evidence found' -- genuine negative searches, with E's search flagged as incomplete (rate-limited) rather than clean. No fundamental flaw was found in the brief's sourcing traceability.
